## Objective

- Understand what an IDE is 
- Features in IDEs that improve productivity and workflow
- VS Code is used for agentic workflows.

## What is an IDE?

Code is just text and can be edited in any text editor. Some languages have their own text editor, with features specific to that language - for example, Stata's do-file editor or RStudio for R.

An IDE is a text editor on steroids. IDEs like VS Code are typically not specific to any one programming language. This means that they have a broader user base. A broader user base makes it more likely that when a new tool is introduced, its developers will first develop support for it within the IDE.

## Why use an IDE? 

AI tools are new and constantly changing, but general IDEs will likely adopt support for these tools more quickly than language-specific editors, making them a more future-proof choice for developers in the AI world.

We think using IDEs like VS Code makes you a better code writer, but the reason it is a requirement to use it in this training is that it gives us access to AI tools no matter what language you work in as a user on a day-to-day basis.

But once you've been forced to use an advanced IDE to get access to AI, you might start wondering how you ever managed without it. :)
